title: Potato from Puerto Rican Beef Stew with Gravy

content.title: About
content.content: The potato used in traditional Puerto Rican beef stew is boiled until tender and served in a savory gravy made from tomatoes, spices, and beef broth. The dish balances the natural sweetness of the potato with the rich, meaty flavor and Caribbean aromatics.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Puerto Rican stew is often cooked in large pots over an open flame, giving it a subtle smoky note.
Potatoes are cut into large cubes so they hold their shape and soak up the sauce.
The stew traditionally includes an “adobo” blend of garlic, oregano, vinegar, and olive oil.
It is commonly served with rice, beans, or crusty bread to mop up the remaining gravy.
In Puerto Rico, potatoes are considered a comfort food, especially during cooler months.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide sustained energy thanks to their high starch content.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and enhances iron absorption from the beef.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: Protein from beef
items.content: The beef adds complete protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Thyme, oregano, and garlic contain compounds that combat free radicals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The gravy can be salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Traditional stew uses a modest amount of fat; it can be reduced if desired.

items.title: Risk of foodborne bacteria
items.content: Ensure the beef is fully cooked and store leftovers properly to avoid food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot with rice, beans, or bread to soak up the gravy. The potatoes can be eaten as a side or mixed throughout the stew. For extra brightness, garnish with fresh cilantro or a squeeze of lime.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the stew to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat thoroughly until boiling to kill any potential bacteria.
